reasoning_content:
The circle has center O and diameter AB. The upper half is divided into several sectors. From the figure: starting from ray OB (right side, 0°), there's a 25° angle between OB and the next ray, then 45° between that ray and the next ray, then the shaded sector, and then a 40° angle between the left boundary of the shaded sector and ray OA (left side, 180°).

Wait, let me look at the figure carefully. The angles shown: 40° is between ray OA and the left boundary of the shaded sector (the arc near the 40° label spans from OA to the left edge of the shaded sector). The 25° is between OB and the first ray above it. The 45° is between that first ray and the second ray (the right boundary of the shaded sector).

So the upper half (180°) is divided as follows: from OB: 25°, then 45°, then the shaded sector angle x, then 40° to OA.

Therefore 25 + 45 + x + 40 = 180 → x = 70°.

Probability = 70/360 = 7/36.

Wait, but let me check the figure: the 45° arc seems to span between the ray at 25° and the ray at 70° (the right boundary of the shaded sector). The 40° arc spans from OA (180°) to the left boundary of the shaded sector (140°). The shaded sector is between 70° and 140°, so 70°.

Therefore probability = 70/360 = 7/36.

Double-check: 25+45=70; 180-40=140; 140-70=70. Yes, shaded angle = 70°.

Probability = 70/360 = 7/36.

Answer: \boxed{7/36}.
content:
Looking at the upper semicircle (180° total), the angles from ray OB to ray OA are: 25°, then 45°, then the shaded sector, then 40°.

Shaded angle = 180° − 25° − 45° − 40° = 70°.

Probability = shaded sector area / whole disk area = 70° / 360° = 7/36.

\boxed{7/36}
